_comment: Single source of truth for the oMLX admin console's design tokens. The web console and the macOS app both read the generated artifacts, never this file directly. Regenerate with `python omlx/admin/build_tokens.py`; CI drift is caught by tests/test_generated_tokens.py.

control._comment: Filled controls. `primary` stays the neutral high-contrast fill (a segmented control's chosen knob, a switch-like plate); `accent` is the console's one filled action colour, and it is the same near-black as `primary` (`#171717`, what the console drew before the token layer and what the project still ships on the branch this series targets): a button that saves and a button that acts wear the same weight, and the blue in the palette stays the *interaction* tint (`semantic.accent` — links, a selected row), never a fill. Hover always moves away from the label's contrast, never below it. `focusRing` is the console's own black: the same value the filled action colour uses in each appearance (`#171717` in the light one, `#e5e5e5` in the dark one), so a keyboard ring reads as part of the palette rather than a tint from outside it; it is a mark rather than text, so 3:1 is the bar. `switchOn` is the black the console already drew in the light appearance and one grey step in the dark one (`#a1a1aa`), so an on switch stays a mark instead of a hole in its track; the knob's position already carries the state, so the fill is a second signal rather than the only one.

semantic._comment: Apple system colors, expressed per appearance so the web console reads the same weight as the native app's status dots. `accent` is the console's one tint — the system blue the HIG tints controls with — and it is what the chat's composer, the settings rail's selected section and every link and focus ring now draw. The other six are status marks only: dots, bars, badges. Nothing decorative is coloured. `teal` and `purple` are here for the log levels the app also draws (see dashboard.js logLevelTone): six levels, six marks, one meaning each.

typography._comment: Six levels, no others. Nothing may render below the auxiliary step (12px); the enhanced-readability switch now only raises contrast, because the floor it used to enforce is the floor of the scale itself.

families.sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Hiragino Sans GB', 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif
families.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

aux.usage: captions, timestamps, table secondary cells, badges

body.usage: body copy, form labels, table primary cells

section.usage: section headings, drawer and sheet titles

space._comment: 8pt grid. 4pt exists only for icon-to-label gaps.

layout._comment: Grid metrics that are part of the layout scale rather than page-local numbers: the console measure, the KPI card minimum width, the heatmap label column, the log viewer columns, row pitch and the height its occurrence list scrolls in, and the settings anchor rail. There is exactly one measure and every page shares it: `widths` is the set the Status tab's layout control offers, `default` is the console's measure out of the box, and the chosen one is applied to the page frame itself — so a wider dashboard widens Settings, Logs, Models and Bench with it. `0` means no limit. `topBarHeight`, `subTabHeight` and `stickyGap` are the three numbers the sticky layers are built from, measured at the default type scale. The page scrolls the window, so a sticky sub-tab row pins at `top: topBarHeight` (right below the top bar), a sticky rail below it at `stickyOffset` = `topBarHeight + subTabHeight + stickyGap`, and a section anchor -- also positioned against the viewport -- clears the same `stickyOffset`.

material._comment: Two translucent layers only: the top bar and the modal scrim. Content surfaces stay solid.

elevation._comment: Micro shadows replace hard borders on cards and popovers.

badge._comment: Badge foregrounds. A tone badge is the system colour at 14% behind its label, which is far too light to carry text, so each appearance names the step that reaches 4.5:1 on its own tint (the console contrast suite measures it). The system colours stay for dots, bars and fills. One tone per log level, so the label and the colour never disagree.

console._comment: Web console only: transition durations and the two overlay widths. The app animates with its own timings, so these never reach DesignTokens.swift.

label._comment: Label colours: the tags and chips that are not log levels — a model profile, a preset, a model type, a cluster state. Each family is a fill plus the step that reaches 4.5:1 on it. These started as Tailwind literals in the markup, which a theme cannot reach; naming them here is what lets the custom-theme feature recolour them. Both appearances name the same values, because the literals they replace did not change with the appearance either.
